newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Two-fifths of Argentine wages under $500/mo -paper.
newsitem.headline: Two-fifths of Argentine wages under $500/mo -paper.

text.p: Two-fifths of Argentina's salary-earners are paid less than $500 a month, according to a government study published in the Clarin newspaper Wednesday.
Some 42.6 percent of Argentine gross salaries are less than $500, according to a Social Security Secretariat survey of employees paying into the national pension system in May quoted by Clarin.
Another 29.8 percent earn between $501 and $1,000, while 12.1 percent are paid between $1,001 and $1,500. Only 15.5 percent of salary-earners are paid more than $1,500 a month.
About 3.7 million workers pay into the national pension system. Another 700,000 employees, who were not included in the survey, pay into provincial pension systems.
The Economy Ministry estimates that another 2.8 million people are working illegally for employers who do not pay their social security contributions.
Argentina has an unemployment rate of 17.3 percent and has been hit by a wave of roadblocks and protests against poverty and joblessness in its provinces.
But the Economy Ministry's chief advisor Carlos Rodriguez defended the government's performance on poverty since the introduction of peso-dollar parity, known as "the Convertibility Plan," in 1991.

"The percentage of (people with) basic needs unsatisfied was 15 percent when Convertibility began, and now it is 12.6 percent. It has not fallen as much as we would have liked but it has dropped, and it was 19 percent in 1988," Rodriguez told the La Nacion daily newspaper Wednesday.
